what: The Newsroom Design Lab: its vaults (published read keys, read only), the three design directions, the screenshots shown on /lab/, and the decisions it exists to settle. Vaults and decisions are copied from the lab hub vault (3bf2p46v, data/vaults.json and data/proposals/decisions.json, v0.1.1).

vaults.title: The lab
vaults.answers: The brief, the three directions, the map from review to prototype, the decisions, the reviews.

vaults.title: Front page & personas
vaults.answers: First visit; a publication with a heart; the purpose page; publication and workshop; personas as the core primitive; the founder mini-site.

vaults.title: Article & reader primitives
vaults.answers: The article page reordered; the short version first; the side column; highlights and notes; ratings that start unselected; ask the article; the reading board; the reader's record.

vaults.title: Findability
vaults.answers: Five desks by audience; 42 controlled tags from 339 raw ones; 11 series with part numbers; linkable search; reading time and format on every card; the Librarian's audit.

directions.label: A · Broadsheet
directions.idea: A serious publication. Editorial hierarchy, one lead, a named author with a stated purpose.
directions.looks: Serif headlines, warm paper, rules between columns, kickers, restrained colour. FT / Guardian long-read feel.

directions.label: B · Briefing
directions.idea: Answers first. Every unit opens with the news in two sentences, then labelled blocks: the news, our view, the evidence, room for disagreement.
directions.looks: Sans, compact cards with reading time and format, bold labels, one accent colour. Semafor / Axios feel.

directions.label: C · Your desk
directions.idea: The reader's own newsroom. The persona is the front page; the board, highlights, notes and questions are first-class.
directions.looks: App-like: left rail, side column, chips and progress. Readwise / Arc feel.

decisions.question: Which direction should the live front page take?
decisions.why: Everything else follows from it: type, density, how much the reader's own data shows.

options.label: Mix: A for the publication, C for a signed-in reader

decisions.question: Which masthead line names the heart?
decisions.why: The tagline today describes a method, not a subject.

options.label: Field notes on AI agents, security and the next generation of publishing, by Dinis Cruz
Open thinking on agentic AI: what to build, how to secure it, and how to ship it

decisions.question: How many doors on the first screen?
decisions.why: Three is easier to choose from; five covers everyone you send links to.

decisions.question: What opens every article?
decisions.why: Readers have three minutes on a phone; the median article is about 4,500 words.

The article with the reader's side column

decisions.question: How should a rating reach you?
decisions.why: Today it stays in the reader's browser unless they send their whole reading.

options.label: One tap, anonymous, with plain consent
One tap, with an optional email for a reply
Kept locally, sent weekly with the reader's consent

decisions.question: Desks by audience or by subject?
decisions.why: Topics today overlap and one holds 38 of 73 articles.

decisions.question: Ship the reading board in the first release?
decisions.why: It gives a returning reader a reason to come back, and it is the most app-like piece.
